correctness.rationale: For a regular marked poset, every source cover is an actual facet. Cover facets incident with a marked endpoint have unit normal; unmarked-to-unmarked cover facets have normal length sqrt(2). Summing shifted clearance inequalities along a marked interval chain gives the stated upper barrier. Conversely, longest-path potentials from marked vertices satisfy every shifted cover inequality whenever all marked-chain barriers hold; paths containing internal marked vertices decompose into marked interval chains. Thus the minimum barrier is feasible. At equality, the shifted facet system is exactly the complete incenter set, and zero total slack on a minimizing chain forces every constituent facet to be tangent.

value.rationale: Marked order polytopes form a broad geometric framework containing classical representation-theoretic examples such as Gelfand--Tsetlin polytopes. The theorem computes a fundamental Euclidean invariant for every bounded regular member and converts a continuous optimization into a finite marked-chain bottleneck. Unlike the ordinary order-polytope height formula, the optimizer depends simultaneously on prescribed marking gaps and chain lengths, and the result also describes all centers, canonical extremal centers, and forced tangent chains. This is a structural family-wide metric theorem rather than a routine calculation on a fixed example.
